criteria.source: LCD L33944 v27, Indications and limitations.

claim.clinical_notes: The patient returns to the wound clinic. Dead tissue was cut away from a 3 cm ulcer on the right ankle down to the fat layer, with the patient seen one on one. This is the fourth debridement, and the treatment plan was reassessed last week. Past medical history was reviewed without changes. The patient is seen for thick toenails. The patient takes apixaban, and a small cut during nail care could bleed heavily. The patient understands the plan and wants to go ahead. Nail care by the patient or family would put the feet at risk. Plan: selective removal of dead tissue from an open wound, first 20 square cm or less; trimming and cleaning of thickened toenails, 1 to 5 nails.

criteria.text: Active wound care (debridement) is covered to remove dead tissue and promote healing, performed with direct one-on-one patient contact, following accepted standards of wound treatment.
criteria.source: LCD L38902 v12, Indications.

criteria.text: How often debridement is done depends on the wound. Frequent repeated debridement requires a documented reassessment of the treatment plan.
criteria.source: LCD L38902 v12, Indications, frequency.

criteria.text: Care must be part of a plan that addresses complicating factors (pressure off-loading, infection, poor circulation, metabolic or nutritional problems), aiming at wound closure or, when healing is not possible, preventing the wound from getting worse.
criteria.source: LCD L38902 v12, Indications.

criteria.text: It is covered for patients on blood thinners when the record documents the significant risk of non-professional foot care.
criteria.source: LCD L33941 v23, Covered indications.

criteria.text: Routine foot care is covered for nerve damage in the feet (without blood-vessel impairment) severe enough that care by a non-professional would put the patient at risk. The record must document loss of protective sensation: no feeling at 2 or more of 5 sites on either foot with the 5.07 Semmes-Weinstein monofilament.
criteria.source: LCD L33941 v23, Covered indications.

criteria.text: Outside these conditions, routine foot care such as nail trimming is not covered (Medicare Benefit Policy Manual, Chapter 15, Section 290, referenced by the LCD).
criteria.source: LCD L33941 v23, Covered indications, reference to benefit policy.

claim.clinical_notes: The patient has neck pain that travels down the right arm. Vital signs are stable. MRI shows a disc herniation at C5-C6 pressing on the right C6 nerve root, matching the exam. Symptoms have lasted 13 weeks despite physical therapy and anti-inflammatory medicine. The patient has chronic neck pain. Neck pain is mild (1/10) and does not limit daily activities. Pain has lasted 11 months despite physical therapy and medication. There is no pain or numbness down the limbs, and imaging shows no fracture, tumor or infection. Plan: epidural steroid injection between the vertebrae, neck or upper back, with imaging guidance; facet joint nerve block injection, neck or upper back, first level.

criteria.text: History, examination and matching imaging must support nerve-root pain (radiculopathy) or neurogenic claudication from a disc herniation, bone spurs or severe disc degeneration narrowing the spinal canal or nerve openings; or pain after spinal surgery (post-laminectomy syndrome); or acute shingles pain.
criteria.source: LCD L33906 v75, Covered indications.

criteria.text: A repeat injection requires documented improvement of at least 50% in pain lasting at least 3 months, or at least 50% improvement in function, compared with the baseline scale.
criteria.source: LCD L33906 v75, Covered indications, repeat injections.

criteria.text: The pain must have lasted at least 4 weeks, with failure of, or inability to tolerate, 4 weeks of non-invasive conservative care. Acute shingles pain that does not respond to conservative care is exempt from the 4-week wait.
criteria.source: LCD L33906 v75, Covered indications.

criteria.text: The pain must be severe enough to greatly affect quality of life or function, measured with an objective pain or function scale before treatment.
criteria.source: LCD L33906 v75, Covered indications.

criteria.text: Injections must be done under CT or fluoroscopic guidance with contrast, unless there is a documented contrast allergy or pregnancy. Interlaminar injections are limited to one level, and transforaminal injections to two levels in one spinal region.
criteria.source: LCD L33906 v75, Covered indications, technique and levels.

criteria.policy_title: Facet joint injections and nerve ablation
criteria.text: The patient must have moderate to severe chronic neck or low back pain, mainly in the spine itself (axial), causing a functional deficit measured on a pain or disability scale.
criteria.source: LCD L33930 v49, Covered indications.

criteria.policy_title: Facet joint injections and nerve ablation
criteria.text: The pain must have lasted at least 3 months, with documented failure of non-invasive conservative care.
criteria.source: LCD L33930 v49, Covered indications.

criteria.policy_title: Facet joint injections and nerve ablation
criteria.text: There must be no untreated nerve-root pain or neurogenic claudication (except from a facet joint cyst), and no other cause of the pain such as fracture, tumor, infection or major deformity.
criteria.source: LCD L33930 v49, Covered indications.

criteria.policy_title: Facet joint injections and nerve ablation
criteria.text: Diagnostic facet procedures are done with the intent of proceeding to radiofrequency ablation at that level if they succeed. A second, confirming diagnostic procedure at the same level must be at least 2 weeks after the first.
criteria.source: LCD L33930 v49, Section A, diagnostic procedures.

criteria.text: The pain must have lasted at least 4 weeks, with failure of, or inability to tolerate, 4 weeks of non-invasive conservative care. Acute shingles pain that does not respond to conservative care is exempt from the 4-week wait.
